title: Health & Wellness Seminar - Pulmonary Nodules: Analysis & Diagnostic Testing
description: Join Dr. Craig Brown , a pulmonary specialist with Northside Hospital Diagnostic Clinic , for this important discussion. Pulmonary nodules can be as innocent as a scar and as small as a crumb, but these crumbs can grow. Only now are we starting to understand how nodules can be analyzed and assessed with greater accuracy. First step is to understand what type of nodule we are dealing with. After this, we need to understand what diagnostic modalities are available so we are able to rapidly and accurately diagnose any potential harmful diseases. The earlier we find these diseases, the easier it is for us to treat them Presented by: Dr. Craig Brown 230 E.E. Butler Parkway Gainesville, GA 30501 | Phone: (770) 532-6206

title: Finance & Administrative Forum
description: Sold Out! Finance & Administrative Forum Reducing Tax Liability & Improving Cash Flow Through Tax Credits Whether you're actively growing, training your team, or simply want to know what you might be leaving on the table, this session will show you where to look and how to claim those credits. Tuesday, August 11 11:45 AM - 1:00 PM Carroll Daniel 330 Main Street SW All Businesses look for ways to reduce their tax liability and improve cash flow. Tax credits are one of the most direct ways to do this; however, most businesses don't know what they qualify for, or are not aware credits exist. Josh Hollum with TaxCredible, the largest submitter to the State of Georgia for the Retaining Tax Credit, breaks down what's available and why so much goes unclaimed. Drawing on work helping businesses reduce tax liability and free up cash flow through state and federal credits, Josh will discuss what qualifies, what doesn't, and how the dollars you recover can help you fund your next hire, invest in your business, or simply let you breath easier at tax time.

location: 2003 male United States Presidential Scholar for the state of Georgia. Afterward, Dr. Hollar enrolled in the Duke University School of Medicine where he received his Doctor of Medicine (M.D.) degree a
description: How is an optician different from an optometrist and when do you need an ophthalmologist? Which eye diseases steal vision silently, which warning signs cannot wait, and what can today’s cataract surgeries really accomplish? In this presentation, ophthalmologist Matthew Hollar, MD, will explore eye health from cataracts, glaucoma, macular degeneration, and retinal emergencies, while revealing the remarkable technologies now preserving and restoring sight. He will also cover on how insurance, consolidation, and corporate ownership are transforming the relationship among patients, physicians, and the businesses that deliver care, what these changes can improve, what they may put at risk, and how you can become a wiser healthcare consumer. Come find out who's really watching your eyes. Presented by: Dr. Matthew Hollar Dr. Matthew Hollar joined the team of comprehensive ophthalmologists at North Georgia Eye Clinic in 2016, specializing in medical and surgical care of the eye. A native of western North Carolina, he and his family have lived north of Atlanta since 1999. title: Small Business Seminar - Expanding Small Business Capabilities through Higher Education Partnerships
description: About the presentation: Small businesses may fail to scale due to lack of access to resources. Often times, partnering with local technical colleges and universities is not included in discussions when exploring options to scale a business. However, technical colleges and universities are a good resource for small businesses seeking talent, development, and funding support. This session will highlight various ways that small businesses can expand capabilities by partnering with higher education institutions to build a talent pipeline, provide upskilling opportunities for current employees, and to pursue research and grant funding. About the speaker: Dr. Shatrela Washington-Hubbard serves as the Swinton A. Griffith III Dean of the Jacobs College of Business & Media at Brenau University. She holds an earned doctor of philosophy in learning, leadership, and organization development from the University of Georgia. Her professional experience includes industry experience in the fields of human resources and education. title: Farm City Breakfast
description: Farm City Breakfast Wednesday November 18, 2026 7:30am North Hall Community Center This event highlights agribusiness is the Hall County area and is a partnership between the UGA/Hall County Extension, Georgia Farm Bureau and the Greater Hall Chamber of Commerce. This years special guest is Ag Commissioner Tyler Harper. Tyler J Harper is Georgia’s 17th Agriculture Commissioner, a 7th generation farmer, a small businessman, and a proud native of rural South Georgia. A lifelong resident of the Peach State, Harper is a champion for Georgia’s #1 industry, the farm families who fuel its success, and all of rural Georgia. He knows that for Georgia’s farmers and producers, agriculture is more than just a job or a hobby – it is our way of life. Harper grows peanuts, cotton, and timber and runs a small cow-calf operation on land that has been in his family for over 100 years in Irwin County, Georgia.
